(4) Profiling of a Child as referred to in paragraph (1) is the processing of Personal Data of a Child in various forms and ways to identify, evaluate, or predict various aspects of the Child.
(5) In the event that profiling is carried out at the request of the Child as referred to in paragraph (3) letter b, the Electronic System Provider shall guarantee the availability of technology and the effective functioning of technical and operational measures to protect the Child from any harmful impact on the Child.

Article 20
(1) In carrying out the obligation to provide information on the minimum age limit of Children who may use its products or services as referred to in Article 2 paragraph (4) letter a, Electronic System Providers shall provide information on the minimum age limit of Children who may use the Products, Services, and Features.
(2) The minimum age limit of Children as referred to in paragraph (1) is at the lowest 3 (three) years of age, with a grouping of Child age ranges that includes:
a. age 3 (three) to 5 (five) years;
b. age 6 (six) to 9 (nine) years;
c. age 10 (ten) to 12 (twelve) years;
d. age 13 (thirteen) to 15 (fifteen) years; and
e. age 16 (sixteen) up to not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age.
(3) In providing information on the minimum age limit of Children and the age ranges of Children who may use its products or services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), Electronic System Providers are required to ensure that the Products, Services, and Features that they develop and/or operate are in accordance with the minimum age limit of Children and the age ranges of Children who use or access, or who may use or access, those Products, Services, and Features.
(4) In ensuring the implementation of the obligation as referred to in paragraph (1), Electronic System Providers shall take into consideration the needs of the Child adjusted to the stages of growth and development based on the minimum age limit of Children and the age ranges of Children as referred to in paragraph (2).
(5) Further provisions on the minimum age limit of Children and the age ranges of Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated in a Ministerial Regulation.

Article 21
(1) Electronic System Providers that require or make it a condition to register or have an account in order to use or access Products, Services, and Features are required to follow the minimum age limit of Children in accordance with the following provisions:
a. a Child under 13 (thirteen) years of age as referred to in Article 20 paragraph (2) letter a, letter b, and letter c may have an account on Products, Services, and Features that are specifically designed to be used or accessed by Children and have a low risk profile, with the consent of the Parent.
b. a Child aged 13 (thirteen) years up to not yet 16 (sixteen) years of age as referred to in Article 20 paragraph (2) letter d may have an account only on Products, Services, and Features that have a low risk profile, with the consent of the Parent.
c. a Child aged 16 (sixteen) years up to not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age as referred to in Article 20 paragraph (2) letter e may have an account for Products, Services, and Features with the consent of the Parent.
(2) Electronic System Providers are required to guarantee the availability of technology and the effective functioning of technical and operational measures for Parents to be able to supervise the use of Products, Services, and Features through the Child's account.

Article 23
(1) In carrying out the obligation to provide a mechanism for reporting misuse of Products, Services, and Features that violates or potentially violates the rights of the Child as referred to in Article 2 paragraph (4) letter c, Electronic System Providers are required to provide the tools, services, or features needed by the Child that can be easily used or accessed by the Child or by the Parent or Guardian of the Child to help the Child exercise the rights of the Child, or to submit a report or complaint concerning problems experienced by the Child related to the Products, Services, and Features.
(2) Electronic System Providers are required to have and apply operational technical measures in following up on the report or complaint as referred to in paragraph (1).
Chapter III: Supervision of the Provision of Electronic Systems in Child Protection
Part One: General

Article 24
(1) Supervision of the implementation of governance of the Provision of Electronic Systems in Child protection as referred to in this Government Regulation is carried out by the Minister.
(2) In carrying out the supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Minister has the authority to:
a. carry out monitoring and/or tracing of the implementation of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems carried out by Electronic System Providers;
b. receive reports or complaints concerning alleged violations of Child protection obligations committed by Electronic System Providers in the Provision of Electronic Systems;
c. carry out examination to follow up on the monitoring and/or tracing as referred to in letter a and/or the report or complaint as referred to in letter b; and
d. carry out control based on the results of the examination as referred to in letter c.

Article 25
(1) Statements, data, information, and/or documents provided and/or submitted by Electronic System Providers for the purposes of carrying out the supervision as referred to in Article 24.
(2) Protection of the statements, data, information, and/or documents as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26
(1) Handling of alleged violations of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems committed by Electronic System Providers is carried out in the following stages:
a. findings of alleged violations of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems; and
b. examination of alleged violations of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems.
(2) Findings of alleged violations of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a may originate from:
a. the results of monitoring and/or tracing as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) letter a; and/or
b. a report or complaint as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) letter b.
(3) Examination of alleged violations of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is based on the findings of alleged violations of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems as referred to in paragraph (2).
(4) The imposition of administrative sanctions is based on the results of the examination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b.
Part Two: Monitoring and/or Tracing

Article 28
(1) Reports or complaints as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b are submitted to the Minister in writing or electronically.
(2) A report as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted by a Person, a Public Body, or a party who knows of an action or deed of an Electronic System Provider that is alleged to have violated, to be violating, or to be going to violate obligations under the provisions of this Government Regulation.
(3) A complaint as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted by a person or a party who feels they have suffered a loss as a result of an action or deed of an Electronic System Provider that is alleged to have violated obligations under the provisions of this Government Regulation.
(4) A report or complaint as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted by attaching complete and correct documents and information concerning:
a. the identity of the person or party lodging the report or complaint;
b. the identity of the Electronic System Provider;
c. the alleged violation of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems that was committed; and
d. statements and/or evidence containing facts, data, or indications of the occurrence of a violation of Child protection obligations in the Provision of Electronic Systems.
(5) The Ministry shall issue a receipt to the person or party who submits the report or complaint.

Part Four: Preliminary Examination

Article 29
(1) The Ministry shall conduct a preliminary examination of the reporting or complaint documents as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (4) within a maximum of 3 (three) working days from the receipt of the report or complaint.
(2) The Ministry shall determine the period for completing the preliminary examination based on:
a. the degree of difficulty of handling the alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems committed by the Electronic System Provider;
b. the number of Children affected or potentially affected as a result of the incident of the alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems committed by the Electronic System Provider; and/or
c. the completeness of the documents and information as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (4).
(3) In the event that the Ministry concludes, based on the results of the preliminary examination, that there are deficiencies in the documents and/or information as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (4), the Ministry shall notify, in writing or electronically, the Person, Public Body, or party that submitted the report, or the person or party that submitted the complaint, to complete the documents and/or information concerned.
(4) In the event that the Ministry concludes, based on the results of the preliminary examination, that clarification, validation, or explanation is required regarding the documents and/or information as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (4), the Ministry shall be authorized to summon the Person, Public Body, or party that submitted the report, or the person or party that submitted the complaint, in order to obtain the necessary statements, data, information, and/or documents.
(5) The examination as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be set out in an official record of the preliminary examination.
(6) In the event that the Ministry concludes, based on the results of the preliminary examination set out in the form of an official record of the preliminary examination, that there is sufficient information to follow up the report or complaint, the Ministry shall conduct a further examination.
(7) In the event that the Ministry concludes, based on the results of the preliminary examination, that there is not sufficient information to follow up the report or complaint, the Ministry shall be authorized to terminate the examination and to deliver a notification, in writing or electronically, to the Person, Public Body, or party that submitted the report, or the person or party that submitted the complaint.
(8) In the event that the Ministry concludes, based on the results of the preliminary examination, that the Ministry is not authorized to follow up the report or complaint, the Ministry shall deliver a notification, in writing or electronically, of the matter concerned to the Person, Public Body, or party that submitted the report, or the person or party that submitted the complaint.
(9) In completing the preliminary examination, the Ministry may:
a. coordinate with ministries/agencies and/or law enforcement institutions related to the object of the examination; and/or
b. seek the opinion of experts relevant to the preliminary examination.
(10) Further provisions on the procedures for the preliminary examination shall be regulated by Ministerial Regulation.

Part Five: Further Examination

Article 31
(1) The Ministry shall summon an Electronic System Provider suspected of committing a violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems by means of a written or electronic notification.
(2) The written notification as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be delivered to the legal domicile address officially registered with the Ministry.
(3) The electronic notification as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be delivered through the electronic mail officially registered with the Ministry and/or other electronic media determined by the Ministry.
(4) In the event that the legal domicile address or electronic mail address of the Electronic System Provider is not officially registered with the Ministry or has changed without official notification to the Ministry, the Ministry shall announce it on the official website of the Ministry, and this shall be deemed a notification letter.

Article 32
(1) The summons of an Electronic System Provider as referred to in Article 31 paragraph (1) shall be made in order to:
a. convey the existence of the alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems;
b. give the Electronic System Provider the opportunity to give statements, a defense, and/or its opinion; and
c. notify the consequences in the form of administrative sanctions that may be imposed for the violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems.
(2) The summons of an Electronic System Provider suspected of committing a violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be made a maximum of 3 (three) times.
(3) In the event that the Electronic System Provider does not attend after being summoned as referred to in paragraph (2), the Electronic System Provider shall be subject to administrative sanctions based on the available evidence and statements, without an examination of the Electronic System Provider being conducted.

Article 33
(1) The examination of an Electronic System Provider suspected of committing a violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems shall be set out in an official record of the further examination.
(2) The examination of a Person, Public Body, expert, or other party giving the statements needed in the further examination shall be set out in an official record of the further examination.

Article 34
In conducting the examination of an alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems, the Ministry may coordinate with ministries/agencies and/or law enforcement institutions related to the object of the examination.

Article 35
(1) The Electronic System Provider must give or submit statements, data, information, and/or documents that are true, accurate, complete, and not misleading in the examination.
(2) In the event that the Electronic System Provider is unable to give or submit statements, data, information, and/or documents at the time of the examination, the Electronic System Provider shall give or submit them at the time determined by the Ministry.
(3) In the event that the Electronic System Provider does not give, does not submit, or refuses to give or submit the statements, data, information, and/or documents needed for the purposes of the examination of the alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems at the time determined by the Ministry, the Ministry shall be authorized to impose administrative sanctions in respect of the alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems based on the available evidence or statements.
(4) The giving or submission of statements, data, information, and/or documents that are untrue, inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading in the examination shall constitute a basis for the Ministry to assess the level of compliance with the performance of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems by the Electronic System Provider and/or to impose heavier administrative sanctions.

Article 36
Further provisions on the further examination, the summoning of Electronic System Providers, and the procedures for the examination as referred to in Article 30 through Article 35 shall be regulated by Ministerial Regulation.

Part Six: Control

Article 38
(1) A violation of the provisions of Article 2, Article 5 paragraph (6), Article 7 paragraph (1) letter a and letter c through letter i, Article 9 paragraph (1), paragraph (2), paragraph (4), and paragraph (5) letter b, Article 10 paragraph (1) and paragraph (3), Article 11, Article 12 paragraph (1) and paragraph (5), Article 13, Article 14, Article 15, Article 16, Article 17, Article 18, Article 19 paragraph (1), Article 20 paragraph (1) and paragraph (3), Article 21 paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), Article 22 paragraph (1), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4), Article 23 paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) The administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. a written warning;
b. an administrative fine;
c. temporary suspension; and/or
d. termination of access.
(3) A violation of the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) may be subject to one or more administrative sanctions.
(4) The Minister shall be authorized to inform or announce to the public the imposition of administrative sanctions on Electronic System Providers through the official website of the Ministry.

Article 39
The types of administrative sanctions and the stages of imposing administrative sanctions for violations as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1) letter b and letter j shall be regulated in the laws and regulations in the field of Personal Data Protection.

Article 40
(1) The administrative sanctions as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) shall be imposed by the Minister.
(2) In imposing the sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), the Minister shall consider:
a. the category of seriousness or lightness of the violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems committed by the Electronic System Provider;
b. the cooperative conduct of the Electronic System Provider in the examination of the alleged violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems committed by the Electronic System Provider; and
c. other aggravating or mitigating factors.
(3) The category of seriousness or lightness of the violation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall be measured by considering:
a. the duration or length of time the violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems occurred;
b. the number of Children affected as a result of the violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems by the Electronic System Provider; and/or
c. the impact of the violation of the obligation to protect Children in the Provision of Electronic Systems on Children and/or the rights of the Child.
[Article 40 paragraph (4) begins with "Tindakan ..." at the foot of PDF p.26 and continues on PDF p.27, outside this range.]
(4) Cooperative action as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is measured by considering:
a. an official notification from the Electronic System Provider regarding a violation of the Child protection obligations in the provision of its Electronic System;
b. the Electronic System Provider providing or submitting statements, data, information, and/or documents that are true, accurate, complete, and not misleading in the examination as referred to in Article 35 paragraph (1); and
c. the attendance of the Electronic System Provider in the examination pursuant to the summons as referred to in Article 32.
(5) Other factors as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c are measured by considering:
a. the actions of the Electronic System Provider in handling the impact or mitigating the risks arising from the violation of the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System, after the violation became known to the Electronic System Provider and before the violation was examined by the Minister; and
b. the history of violations of the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System committed by the Electronic System Provider.
(6) In considering the factors as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, letter b, and letter c, the Minister may coordinate with the relevant ministries/agencies.
(7) The imposition of administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) does not extinguish criminal and/or civil liability.

Article 41
(1) The Minister shall impose an administrative sanction in the form of a written warning as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter a where, based on the results of the examination, it is concluded that:
a. the violation of the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System committed by the Electronic System Provider falls within the minor category based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (3);
b. the Electronic System Provider is cooperative in the examination of the alleged violation of the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (4); and
c. the mitigating other factors outnumber the aggravating factors based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (5).
(2) In addition to the authority as referred to in paragraph (1), the Minister is authorized to impose an administrative sanction in the form of a written warning as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter a containing an order to the Electronic System Provider to take certain actions in order to fulfil the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System.
(3) The administrative sanction in the form of a written warning is imposed at most 2 (two) times.
(4) Where the administrative sanction in the form of a written warning is imposed at most 2 (two) times as referred to in paragraph (3), the period between the first written warning and the second written warning is 7 (seven) working days.
(5) Where the Minister imposes an administrative sanction accompanied by an order to the Electronic System Provider to take certain actions in order to fulfil the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System, the Minister is authorized to determine the period of the first written warning and the second written warning.

Article 42
(1) The Minister shall impose an administrative sanction in the form of an administrative fine as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter b where, based on the results of the examination, it is concluded that the Electronic System Provider:
a. does not comply with the second written warning as referred to in Article 41; or
b. meets the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (2), which include:
1. the violation committed by the Electronic System Provider falls within the serious category based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (3);
2. the Electronic System Provider is not cooperative based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (4); and/or
3. the aggravating other factors outnumber the mitigating factors based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (5).
(2) The amount of the administrative fine and the procedure for calculating the administrative fine are carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of non-tax state revenue.
(3) In imposing the administrative sanction in the form of an administrative fine as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter b, the Minister is authorized to give an order to the Electronic System Provider to take certain actions in order to fulfil the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System.

Article 43
(1) The Minister shall impose an administrative sanction in the form of temporary suspension as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter c where, based on the results of the examination, it is concluded that the Electronic System Provider:
a. does not fulfil the obligation to pay the administrative fine as referred to in Article 42; and/or
b. meets the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (2), which include:
1. the violation of obligations committed by the Electronic System Provider falls within the serious category based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (3);
2. the Electronic System Provider is not cooperative based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (4); and/or
3. the aggravating other factors outnumber the mitigating factors based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (5).
(2) The temporary suspension as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out against the Product, Service, and/or Feature.
(3) The period of the temporary suspension as referred to in paragraph (1) is determined by the Minister.
(4) In imposing the administrative sanction in the form of temporary suspension as referred to in paragraph (1), the Minister is authorized to give an order to the Electronic System Provider to take certain actions in order to fulfil the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System.
(5) In determining the period of the temporary suspension, the Minister considers the period of effort of the Electronic System Provider to carry out the order as referred to in paragraph (4).

Article 44
(1) The Minister shall impose an administrative sanction in the form of termination of access as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter d where, based on the results of the examination, it is concluded that the Electronic System Provider:
a. does not fulfil the obligation to pay the administrative fine as referred to in Article 42;
b. does not comply with the order as referred to in article 43 paragraph (4); and/or
c. meets the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (2), which include:
1. the violation committed by the Electronic System Provider falls within the serious category based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (3);
2. the Electronic System Provider is not cooperative based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (4); and/or
3. the aggravating other factors outnumber the mitigating factors based on the considerations as referred to in Article 40 paragraph (5).
(2) Where the Minister imposes the administrative sanction of termination of access, the Minister may:
a. coordinate with the ministries/agencies that are the regulating and supervising authority of the sector concerning the Electronic System Provider; and/or
b. request the opinion of experts relevant to the examination of the alleged violation of the Child protection obligations in the provision of the Electronic System committed by the Electronic System Provider.
Part Two: Entry into Force and Delivery of Decisions Imposing Administrative Sanctions

Article 45
(1) The decision imposing an administrative sanction takes effect on the date it is issued.
(2) The decision on an administrative sanction may set the time limits for the commencement and the end of the imposition of the administrative sanction.
(3) The decision on an administrative sanction is issued on a working day.
(4) The imposition of an administrative sanction may be issued on a day other than a working day due to urgent circumstances and/or other legitimate interests, such that it cannot be postponed to the next working day.

Article 46
(1) The decision imposing an administrative sanction is delivered to the Electronic System Provider in writing or electronically.
(2) The decision as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delivered to other interested parties.
(3) Where the legal domicile address or the electronic mail address of the Electronic System Provider is not officially registered with the Ministry or has changed without official notification to the Ministry, the Ministry shall announce it on the official website of the Ministry.

Article 47
(1) An Electronic System Provider that feels aggrieved as a result of the imposition of an administrative sanction may submit an objection to the Minister.
(2) The submission of an objection as referred to in paragraph (1) does not postpone the implementation of the decision.
(3) The Minister shall resolve the objection submitted by the Electronic System Provider as referred to in paragraph (1).
(4) Where the objection as referred to in paragraph (1) is accepted, the Minister shall issue a decision in accordance with the objection petition.
(5) Where the Electronic System Provider does not accept the resolution of the objection as referred to in paragraph (1), the Electronic System Provider may file a lawsuit with the state administrative court to assess whether or not there is an element of abuse of authority in the decision and/or action.
(6) Further provisions on the procedure for submitting objections as referred to in paragraph (1) up to paragraph (4) are regulated in a Ministerial Regulation.
Chapter V: Participation of Ministries/Agencies and the Public

Article 48
(1) Ministries/agencies coordinate in accordance with the duties, functions, and authorities regulated in laws and regulations in:
a. raising public awareness of the benefits and negative impacts of the use of Products, Services, and Features;
b. providing integrated services for Children to provide Child protection in the provision of Electronic Systems; and
c. conducting supervision of Child protection.
(2) The Parent or Guardian of the Child, and the public, have a role in supervising the implementation of Child protection in the provision of Electronic Systems.
(3) The role of the Parent or Guardian of the Child as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. helping the Child to choose Products, Services, and Features that are appropriate to the Child's age and needs;
b. assessing the suitability of the Products, Services, and Features for the age of the Child who will use them before giving consent;
c. monitoring the use of Products, Services, and Features; and
d. providing education to the Child on the benefits and negative impacts of the use of Products, Services, and Features.
(4) The role of the public as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. providing education to Children, Parents, or Guardians of Children, at a minimum on the benefits and negative impacts of the use of Products, Services, and Features; and
b. reporting or complaining about alleged violations of the Child protection obligations in the provision of Electronic Systems committed by Electronic System Providers.
Chapter VI: Transitional Provisions

Article 49
When this Government Regulation comes into force, Electronic System Providers and other parties related to the provision of Products, Services, and Features are required to adjust to the governance provisions under this Government Regulation within a maximum of 2 (two) years from the promulgation of this Government Regulation.
Chapter VII: Closing Provisions

Article 50
This Government Regulation comes into force on the date of its promulgation.
In order that everyone may know of it, it is ordered that this Government Regulation be promulgated by placing it in the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 1
In this Law, the following definitions apply:
1. Personal Data means data about an individual who is identified or can be identified, either individually or in combination with other information, whether directly or indirectly, through an electronic or non-electronic system.
2. Personal Data Protection means the entirety of efforts to protect Personal Data in the series of Personal Data processing in order to guarantee the constitutional rights of the Personal Data Subject.
3. Information means statements, declarations, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts, or their explanations, that can be seen, heard, and read, presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology, whether electronically or non-electronically.
4. Personal Data Controller means every person, public body, and international organization acting individually or jointly in determining the purposes of and exercising control over the processing of Personal Data.
5. Personal Data Processor means every person, public body, and international organization acting individually or jointly in carrying out the processing of Personal Data on behalf of the Personal Data Controller.
6. Personal Data Subject means an individual to whom Personal Data is attached.
7. Every Person means an individual or a corporation.
8. Corporation means an organized collection of persons and/or assets, whether incorporated or unincorporated.
9. Public Body means executive, legislative, and judicial agencies, and other bodies whose principal functions and duties relate to the administration of the state, which are funded in part or in whole from the State Revenue and Expenditure Budget and/or the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, or non-governmental organizations insofar as they are funded in part or in whole from the State Revenue and Expenditure Budget and/or the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, public donations, and/or from abroad.
10. International Organization means an organization recognized as a subject of international law and having the capacity to make international agreements.
11. Central Government, hereinafter referred to as the Government, means the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the power of government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 2
(1) This Law applies to Every Person, Public Body, and International Organization that performs legal acts as regulated in this Law:
a. that are located within the jurisdiction of the State of the Republic of Indonesia; and
b. outside the jurisdiction of the State of the Republic of Indonesia, that have legal consequences:
1. within the jurisdiction of the State of the Republic of Indonesia; and/or
2. for Personal Data Subjects who are Indonesian citizens outside the jurisdiction of the State of the Republic of Indonesia.
(2) This Law does not apply to the processing of Personal Data by individuals in the course of personal or household activities.

Chapter II: Principles

Article 5
A Personal Data Subject has the right to obtain Information about the clarity of identity, the basis of legal interest, the purpose of the request for and use of Personal Data, and the accountability of the party requesting Personal Data.

Article 6
A Personal Data Subject has the right to complete, update, and/or correct errors and/or inaccuracies in Personal Data about himself/herself in accordance with the purpose of the processing of Personal Data.

Article 7
A Personal Data Subject has the right to obtain access to and obtain a copy of Personal Data about himself/herself in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

Article 8
A Personal Data Subject has the right to terminate the processing of, erase, and/or destroy Personal Data about himself/herself in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

Article 9
A Personal Data Subject has the right to withdraw consent to the processing of Personal Data about himself/herself that has been given to the Personal Data Controller.

Article 10
(1) A Personal Data Subject has the right to object to decision-making actions that are based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that give rise to legal consequences or have a significant impact on the Personal Data Subject.
(2) Further provisions on the lodging of objections to automated processing as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in a Government Regulation.

Article 11
A Personal Data Subject has the right to delay or restrict the processing of Personal Data proportionally in accordance with the purpose of the processing of Personal Data.

Article 12
(1) A Personal Data Subject has the right to sue and to receive compensation for violations of the processing of Personal Data about himself/herself in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.
(2) Further provisions on violations of the processing of Personal Data and the procedures for imposing compensation as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in a Government Regulation.

Article 13
(1) A Personal Data Subject has the right to obtain and/or use Personal Data about himself/herself from the Personal Data Controller in a form that conforms to a structure and/or format commonly used or readable by electronic systems.
(2) A Personal Data Subject has the right to use and transmit Personal Data about himself/herself to another Personal Data Controller, insofar as the systems used can communicate with each other securely in accordance with the principles of Personal Data Protection under this Law.
(3) Further provisions on the right of Personal Data Subjects to use and transmit Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated in a Government Regulation.

Article 14
The exercise of the rights of Personal Data Subjects as referred to in Article 6 through Article 11 is submitted through a recorded request delivered electronically or non-electronically to the Personal Data Controller.

Article 17
(1) The installation of visual data processing or handling devices in public places and/or at public service facilities is carried out subject to the following provisions:
a. it is for the purposes of security, disaster prevention, and/or the administration of traffic or the collection, analysis, and management of traffic Information;
b. it must display Information in the area where the visual data processing or handling devices have been installed; and
c. it is not used to identify a person.
(2) The provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b and letter c are excluded for the prevention of criminal acts and law enforcement processes in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

Article 18
(1) The Processing of Personal Data may be carried out by 2 (two) or more Personal Data Controllers.
(2) Where the Processing of Personal Data is carried out by 2 (two) or more Personal Data Controllers, the following minimum requirements must be met:
a. there is an agreement between the Personal Data Controllers that sets out the roles, responsibilities, and relationship among the Personal Data Controllers;
b. there are mutually related purposes and a manner of Personal Data processing that are determined jointly; and
c. there is a contact person who is designated jointly.

Chapter VI: Obligations of Personal Data Controllers and Personal Data Processors in the Processing of Personal Data

Part One: General

Article 19
Personal Data Controllers and Personal Data Processors include:
a. Any Person;
b. Public Bodies; and
c. International Organizations.

Part Two: Obligations of Personal Data Controllers

Article 22
(1) Consent to the processing of Personal Data is given through written or recorded consent.
(2) Consent as referred to in paragraph (1) may be given electronically or non-electronically.
(3) Consent as referred to in paragraph (1) has the same legal force.
(4) Where the consent as referred to in paragraph (1) contains other purposes, the request for consent must comply with the following provisions:
a. it can be clearly distinguished from other matters;
b. it is made in a format that is understandable and easily accessible; and
c. it uses simple and clear language.
(5) Consent that does not comply with the provisions referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (4) is declared null and void by law.

Article 23
A contractual clause containing a request for the processing of Personal Data that does not include valid explicit consent from the Data Subject is declared null and void by law.

Article 24
In carrying out the processing of Personal Data, the Personal Data Controller must show proof of the consent that has been given by the Data Subject.

Article 25
(1) The processing of the Personal Data of a child is carried out specifically.
(2) The processing of the Personal Data of a child as referred to in paragraph (1) must obtain the consent of the child's parent and/or the child's guardian in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26
(1) The processing of the Personal Data of persons with disabilities is carried out specifically.
(2) The processing of the Personal Data of persons with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through communication using certain means in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The processing of the Personal Data of persons with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (2) must obtain the consent of the person with a disability and/or the guardian of the person with a disability in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 27
A Personal Data Controller must carry out the processing of Personal Data in a limited and specific manner, lawfully, and transparently.

Article 28
A Personal Data Controller must carry out the processing of Personal Data in accordance with the purpose of the processing of Personal Data.

Article 29
(1) A Personal Data Controller must ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of Personal Data in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) In ensuring the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1), the Personal Data Controller must carry out verification.

Article 30
(1) A Personal Data Controller must update and/or correct errors and/or inaccuracies in Personal Data no later than 3 x 24 (three times twenty-four) hours from the time the Personal Data Controller receives the request to update and/or correct the Personal Data.
(2) The Personal Data Controller must notify the Data Subject of the result of the update and/or correction of the Personal Data.

Article 31
A Personal Data Controller must make a record of all Personal Data processing activities.

Article 32
(1) A Personal Data Controller must provide the Data Subject with access to the Personal Data that is processed, together with the track record of the processing of the Personal Data, in accordance with the retention period of the Personal Data.
(2) The access referred to in paragraph (1) is provided no later than 3 x 24 (three times twenty-four) hours from the time the Personal Data Controller receives the access request.

Article 33
A Personal Data Controller must refuse to give the Data Subject access to changes to Personal Data where:
a. it endangers the security, physical health, or mental health of the Data Subject and/or of another person;
b. it has an impact on the disclosure of the Personal Data of another person; and/or
c. it is contrary to the interests of national defence and security.

Article 35
A Personal Data Controller must protect and ensure the security of the Personal Data that it processes, by carrying out:
a. the formulation and implementation of operational technical measures to protect Personal Data from interference in the processing of Personal Data that is contrary to the provisions of laws and regulations; and
b. the determination of the security level of Personal Data having regard to the nature and risk of the Personal Data that must be protected in the processing of Personal Data.

Article 36
In carrying out the processing of Personal Data, the Personal Data Controller must maintain the confidentiality of Personal Data.

Article 37
A Personal Data Controller must supervise every party involved in the processing of Personal Data under the control of the Personal Data Controller.

Article 38
A Personal Data Controller must protect Personal Data from unauthorized processing.

Article 39
(1) A Personal Data Controller must prevent Personal Data from being accessed without authorization.
(2) The prevention referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by using a security system for the Personal Data that is processed and/or by processing Personal Data using an Electronic System in a reliable, secure, and accountable manner.
(3) The prevention referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 40
(1) A Personal Data Controller must stop the processing of Personal Data where the Data Subject withdraws consent to the processing of Personal Data.
(2) The stopping of the processing of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out no later than 3 x 24 (three times twenty-four) hours from the time the Personal Data Controller receives the request to withdraw consent to the processing of Personal Data.

Article 41
(1) A Personal Data Controller must carry out the postponement and restriction of the processing of Personal Data, whether in part or in whole, no later than 3 x 24 (three times twenty-four) hours from the time the Personal Data Controller receives the request for postponement and restriction of the processing of Personal Data.
(2) The postponement and restriction of the processing of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) are excepted where:
a. there are provisions of laws and regulations that do not allow the postponement and restriction of the processing of Personal Data;
b. it may endanger the safety of other parties; and/or
c. the Data Subject is bound by a written agreement with the Personal Data Controller that does not allow the postponement and restriction of the processing of Personal Data.
(3) The Personal Data Controller must notify the Data Subject that the postponement and restriction of the processing of Personal Data has been carried out.

Article 42
(1) A Personal Data Controller must terminate the processing of Personal Data where:
a. the retention period has been reached;
b. the purpose of the processing of Personal Data has been achieved; or
c. there is a request from the Data Subject.
(2) The termination of the processing of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 43
(1) A Personal Data Controller must delete Personal Data where:
a. the Personal Data is no longer needed for the achievement of the purpose of the processing of Personal Data;
b. the Data Subject has withdrawn consent to the processing of Personal Data;
c. there is a request from the Data Subject; or
d. the Personal Data was obtained and/or processed unlawfully.
(2) The deletion of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 44
(1) A Personal Data Controller must destroy Personal Data where:
a. its retention period has expired and it is designated for destruction based on the archive retention schedule;
b. there is a request from the Data Subject;
c. it is not related to the settlement of the legal process of a case; and/or
d. the Personal Data was obtained and/or processed unlawfully.
(2) The destruction of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 45
The Personal Data Controller must notify the Data Subject of the deletion and/or destruction of Personal Data.

Article 46
(1) In the event of a failure of Personal Data Protection, the Personal Data Controller must submit a written notification no later than 3 x 24 (three times twenty-four) hours to:
a. the Data Subject; and
b. the Institution.
(2) The written notification as referred to in paragraph (1) must contain at a minimum:
a. the Personal Data that was disclosed;
b. when and how the Personal Data was disclosed; and
c. the efforts to handle and recover from the disclosure of the Personal Data by the Personal Data Controller.
(3) In certain cases, the Personal Data Controller must notify the public of the failure of Personal Data Protection.

Article 47
The Personal Data Controller must be responsible for the processing of Personal Data and must demonstrate accountability in fulfilling its obligations to implement the principles of Personal Data Protection.

Article 48
(1) A Personal Data Controller in the form of a legal entity that carries out a merger, split-off, acquisition, consolidation, or dissolution of the legal entity must submit a notification of the transfer of Personal Data to the Data Subject.
(2) The notification of the transfer of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is made before and after the merger, split-off, acquisition, consolidation, or dissolution of the legal entity.
(3) In the event that a Personal Data Controller in the form of a legal entity carries out a dissolution or is dissolved, the storage, transfer, deletion, or destruction of Personal Data is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) The storage, transfer, deletion, or destruction of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (3) is notified to the Data Subject.
(5) Further provisions on the procedures for the notification as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (4) are regulated in a Government Regulation.

Article 49
The Personal Data Controller and/or Personal Data Processor must carry out the orders of the Institution in the context of implementing Personal Data Protection in accordance with this Law.

Article 50
(1) The obligations of the Personal Data Controller as referred to in Article 30, Article 32, Article 36, Article 42, Article 43 paragraph (1) letter a up to and including letter c, Article 44 paragraph (1) letter b, Article 45, and Article 46 paragraph (1) letter a, are exempted for:
a. the interests of national defense and security;
b. the interests of law enforcement processes;
c. the public interest in the context of state administration; or
d. the interests of supervision of the financial services sector, monetary matters, the payment system, and financial system stability carried out in the context of state administration.
(2) The exemption as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out only in the context of implementing the provisions of the Law.

Part Three: Obligations of the Personal Data Processor

Article 51
(1) In the event that the Personal Data Controller appoints a Personal Data Processor, the Personal Data Processor must carry out the processing of Personal Data based on the order of the Personal Data Controller.
(2) The processing of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions regulated in this Law.
(3) The processing of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1) is included within the responsibility of the Personal Data Controller.
(4) The Personal Data Processor may involve another Personal Data Processor in carrying out the processing of Personal Data.
(5) The Personal Data Processor must obtain written consent from the Personal Data Controller before involving another Personal Data Processor as referred to in paragraph (4).
(6) In the event that the Personal Data Processor carries out the processing of Personal Data outside the order and purposes set by the Personal Data Controller, the processing of Personal Data becomes the responsibility of the Personal Data Processor.

Article 52
The provisions on the obligations of the Personal Data Controller as referred to in Article 29, Article 31, Article 35, Article 36, Article 37, Article 38, and Article 39 also apply to the Personal Data Processor.
Part Four: Officials or Officers Who Carry Out the Personal Data Protection Function

Article 53
(1) The Personal Data Controller and the Personal Data Processor must appoint an official or officer who carries out the Personal Data Protection function in the event that:
a. the processing of Personal Data is for the purposes of public service;
b. the core activities of the Personal Data Controller are of a nature, scope, and/or purpose that requires regular and systematic monitoring of Personal Data on a large scale; and
c. the core activities of the Personal Data Controller consist of the processing of Personal Data on a large scale for specific Personal Data and/or Personal Data relating to criminal acts.
(2) The official or officer who carries out the Personal Data Protection function as referred to in paragraph (1) is appointed on the basis of professionalism, knowledge of the law, Personal Data Protection practices, and the ability to fulfil their duties.
(3) The official or officer who carries out the Personal Data Protection function as referred to in paragraph (2) may come from inside and/or outside the Personal Data Controller or the Personal Data Processor.

Article 54
(1) The official or officer who carries out the Personal Data Protection function has duties of at least:
a. informing and giving advice to the Personal Data Controller or the Personal Data Processor so that they comply with the provisions in this Law;
b. monitoring and ensuring compliance with this Law and the policies of the Personal Data Controller or the Personal Data Processor;
c. giving advice on the Personal Data Protection impact assessment and monitoring the performance of the Personal Data Controller and the Personal Data Processor; and
d. coordinating and acting as a contact person for issues relating to the processing of Personal Data.
(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the official or officer who carries out the Personal Data Protection function must pay attention to the risks associated with the processing of Personal Data, taking into account the nature, scope, context, and purposes of the processing.
(3) Further provisions on the official or officer who carries out the Personal Data Protection function are regulated in a Government Regulation.

Chapter VII: Transfer of Personal Data

Part One: Transfer of Personal Data Within the Jurisdiction of the Republic of Indonesia

Article 55
(1) The Personal Data Controller may transfer Personal Data to another Personal Data Controller within the jurisdiction of the Republic of Indonesia.
(2) The Personal Data Controller that transfers Personal Data and the one that receives the transfer of Personal Data must carry out Personal Data Protection as referred to in this Law.

Part Two: Transfer of Personal Data Outside the Jurisdiction of the Republic of Indonesia

Article 56
(1) The Personal Data Controller may transfer Personal Data to a Personal Data Controller and/or Personal Data Processor outside the jurisdiction of the Republic of Indonesia in accordance with the provisions regulated in this Law.
(2) In carrying out the transfer of Personal Data as referred to in paragraph (1), the Personal Data Controller must ensure that the country where the Personal Data Controller and/or Personal Data Processor receiving the transfer of Personal Data is domiciled has a level of Personal Data Protection that is equal to or higher than that regulated in this Law.
(3) In the event that the provisions as referred to in paragraph (2) are not fulfilled, the Personal Data Controller must ensure that there is adequate and binding Personal Data Protection.
(4) In the event that the provisions as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) are not fulfilled, the Personal Data Controller must obtain the consent of the Data Subject.
(5) Further provisions on the transfer of Personal Data are regulated in a Government Regulation.
Chapter VIII: Administrative Sanctions

Article 57
(1) Violation of the provisions of Article 20 paragraph (1), Article 21, Article 24, Article 25 paragraph (2), Article 26 paragraph (3), Article 27, Article 28, Article 29, Article 30, Article 31, Article 32 paragraph (1), Article 33, Article 34 paragraph (1), Article 35, Article 36, Article 37, Article 38, Article 39 paragraph (1), Article 40 paragraph (1), Article 41 paragraph (1) and paragraph (3), Article 42 paragraph (1), Article 43 paragraph (1), Article 44 paragraph (1), Article 45, Article 46 paragraph (1) and paragraph (3), Article 47, Article 48 paragraph (1), Article 49, Article 51 paragraph (1) and paragraph (5), Article 52, Article 53 paragraph (1), Article 55 paragraph (2), and Article 56 paragraph (2) up to and including paragraph (4) is subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) The administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) take the form of:
a. written warning;
b. temporary suspension of Personal Data processing activities;
c. deletion or destruction of Personal Data; and/or
d. administrative fine.
(3) The administrative sanction in the form of an administrative fine as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is at most 2 (two) percent of annual income or annual revenue in relation to the violation variable.
(4) The imposition of administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by the Institution.
(5) Further provisions on the procedures for imposing administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Government Regulation.
Chapter IX: Institutional Arrangements

Article 58
(1) The Government plays a role in realizing the implementation of Personal Data Protection in accordance with the provisions of this Law.
(2) The implementation of Personal Data Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Institution.
(3) The Institution as referred to in paragraph (2) is established by the President.
(4) The Institution as referred to in paragraph (2) is accountable to the President.
(5) Further provisions on the Institution as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by a Presidential Regulation.

Article 61
Provisions on the procedures for exercising the authority of the institution as referred to in Article 60 shall be regulated in a Government Regulation.

Chapter X: International Cooperation

Article 62
(1) International cooperation shall be carried out by the Government with the governments of other countries or International Organizations in relation to Personal Data Protection.
(2) International cooperation in the context of implementing this Law shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the principles of international law.

Chapter XI: Public Participation

Article 63
(1) The public may play a role, either directly or indirectly, in supporting the implementation of Personal Data Protection.
(2) The exercise of the role as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through education, training, advocacy, socialization, and/or supervision in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
Chapter XII: Dispute Resolution and Procedural Law

Article 64
(1) The resolution of Personal Data Protection disputes shall be carried out through arbitration, the courts, or other alternative dispute resolution institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) The procedural law applicable in the resolution of disputes and/or judicial processes of Personal Data Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out based on the applicable procedural law in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Valid evidence under this Law shall include:
a. evidence as referred to in procedural law; and
b. other evidence in the form of electronic information and/or electronic documents in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Where necessary to protect Personal Data, court proceedings shall be conducted in closed session.

Chapter XIII: Prohibitions in the Use of Personal Data

Article 65
(1) Every Person is prohibited from unlawfully obtaining or collecting Personal Data that does not belong to them with the intent to benefit themselves or another person, which may result in loss to the Data Subject.
(2) Every Person is prohibited from unlawfully disclosing Personal Data that does not belong to them.
(3) Every Person is prohibited from unlawfully using Personal Data that does not belong to them.

Article 66
Every Person is prohibited from creating false Personal Data or falsifying Personal Data with the intent to benefit themselves or another person, which may result in loss to another person.

Chapter XIV: Criminal Provisions

Article 67
(1) Every Person who intentionally and unlawfully obtains or collects Personal Data that does not belong to them with the intent to benefit themselves or another person, which may result in loss to the Data Subject as referred to in Article 65 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 5 (five) years and/or a fine of a maximum of Rp5,000,000,000.00 (five billion rupiah).
(2) Every Person who intentionally and unlawfully discloses Personal Data that does not belong to them as referred to in Article 65 paragraph (2) shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 4 (four) years and/or a fine of a maximum of Rp4,000,000,000.00 (four billion rupiah).
(3) Every Person who intentionally and unlawfully uses Personal Data that does not belong to them as referred to in Article 65 paragraph (3) shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 5 (five) years and/or a fine of a maximum of Rp5,000,000,000.00 (five billion rupiah).

Article 68
Every Person who intentionally creates false Personal Data or falsifies Personal Data with the intent to benefit themselves or another person, which may result in loss to another person as referred to in Article 66, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) years and/or a fine of a maximum of Rp6,000,000,000.00 (six billion rupiah).

Article 69
In addition to being sentenced to the punishments as referred to in Article 67 and Article 68, an additional punishment may also be imposed in the form of confiscation of profits and/or assets obtained from or the proceeds of the criminal offense, and payment of compensation.

Article 71
(1) Where the court imposes a sentence of a fine, the convicted person shall be given a period of 1 (one) month from the time the decision has obtained permanent legal force to pay the fine.
(2) Where there are strong grounds, the period as referred to in paragraph (1) may be extended for a maximum of 1 (one) month.
(3) Where the convicted person does not pay the fine within the period as referred to in paragraph (1) or paragraph (2), the convicted person's assets or income may be seized and auctioned by the public prosecutor to settle the unpaid fine.
(4) Where the seizure and auction of assets or income as referred to in paragraph (3) are insufficient or cannot be carried out, the unpaid fine shall be replaced with imprisonment for a maximum period as threatened for the criminal offense concerned.
(5) The length of the imprisonment as referred to in paragraph (4), as determined by the judge, shall be stated in the court decision.

Article 72
(1) Where the seizure and auction of assets or income as referred to in Article 71 paragraph (4) are carried out against a convicted Corporation and are insufficient to settle the fine, the Corporation shall be subject to a substitute punishment in the form of suspension of part or all of the Corporation's business activities for a maximum period of 5 (five) years.
(2) The length of the suspension of part or all of the Corporation's business activities as referred to in paragraph (1), as determined by the judge, shall be stated in the court decision.

Article 73
The provisions as referred to in Article 71 and Article 72 shall also apply to the imposition of the additional punishment in the form of payment of compensation.

Chapter XV: Transitional Provisions

Article 74
At the time this Law comes into force, Personal Data Controllers, Personal Data Processors, and other parties related to the processing of Personal Data are required to bring themselves into conformity with the provisions on Personal Data processing under this Law within a maximum of 2 (two) years from the promulgation of this Law.

Article 75
At the time this Law comes into force, all provisions of laws and regulations that regulate Personal Data Protection are declared to remain in force insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

Chapter XVI: Closing Provisions

Article 76
This Law comes into force on the date of its promulgation.
For the information of every person, the promulgation of this Law is hereby ordered by its placement in the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 1:
These Regulations are drafted on the basis of laws such as the PRC Law on Protection of Minors, PRC Cybersecurity Law, and PRC Personal Information Protection Law, in order to create an online environment that is beneficial to minors' physical and psychological wellbeing and to safeguard the lawful rights and interests of minors.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 2:
Efforts to protect minors online shall uphold the leadership of the Communist Part of China, be guided by the Core Socialist Values, adhere to the principle of the best interest of the minors, and be suited to the healthy physical and psychological development of minors and the rules and traits of cyberspace, and shall implement joint social governance.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 3:
The State Internet Information Office is responsible for planning and coordinating efforts to protect minors online, and completing efforts based on its duties.
The state department of press, publication, and film and the relevant State Council departments such as for education, communications, public security, civil affairs culture and tourism, health, market regulation, and radio and television, are to complete efforts on the online protection of minors based on their respective duties.
Local people's governments at the county level or above and their relevant departments are responsible for planning and coordinating efforts to protect minors online, and completing efforts based on their respective duties.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 4:
The Communist Youth League, women's federations, trade unions, Disabled Persons Federations, Working Committees for the Care of the Next Generation, youth federations, students' federations, young pioneers' organizations, and other people's organizations as well as relevant social organizations and basic-level mass autonomous organizations, are to assist the relevant departments in efforts on the protection of minors online, and preservation of minors' lawful rights and interests.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 5:
Schools and families shall teach and lead minors to participate in activities that are conducive to their physical and psychological health, and to use the networks rationally, civilly, safely, and reasonably, and shall prevent and intervene in minors' internet addiction.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 6:
Online product and service providers, personal information handlers, and the manufacturers or sellers of smart terminals shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions, and shall respect social mores, comply with professional ethics, be truthful and credible, perform obligations on the protection of minors online, and take social responsibility.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 7:
Online product and service providers, personal information handlers, and the manufacturers or sellers of smart terminals shall accept government and societal oversight, cooperate with relevant departments lawfully carrying out oversight inspections involving efforts to protect minors online; establish convenient, reasonable, and effective channels for complaints and reports, disclose the routes and methods for making complaints and reports in a conspicuous manner, and promptly accept and address complaints and reports from the public.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 8:
Where any organization or individual discovers violations of these Regulations, they may make a complaint or report to relevant departments such as for internet information, press, publication, film, education, communication, public security, civil affairs, culture and tourism, health, market administration, or radio and television. Departments receiving complaints or reports shall promptly handle them in accordance with law; where these do not fall within the responsibilities of that department, they shall promptly transfer the matters to the department empowered to handle them.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 9:
Relevant network industry organizations shall strengthen industry self-discipline, drafting industry specifications on the protection of minors online and guiding members to perform obligations to protect minors online, to strengthen the protection of minors online.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 10:
News media shall use methods such as news channels, special columns (programs), and public interest advertisements to carry out publicity on the laws, regulations, policy measures, and example cases about the protection of minors online and related knowledge, and conduct public opinion guidance on behaviors harming the lawful rights and interests of minors, guiding all of society to jointly participate in the protection of minors online.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 11:
The state encourages and supports the strengthening of scientific research and personnel cultivation in the area of online protections for minors, and the carrying out of international exchanges and cooperation.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 12:
Organizations and individuals making outstanding contributions in efforts on the protection of minors online will be given commendations and awards in accordance with relevant state regulations.
Chapter II: Promotion of Internet Literacy

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 13:
The State Council departments for education shall include internet literacy in school character development education, and, in conjunction with the State Internet Information Office, formulate indexes for evaluating minors' internet literacy.
The departments for education shall guide and support schools in developing online literacy education for minors, focusing on forming awareness of online ethics, cultivating an understanding of online law, building capacity to use the networks, protecting one's person and property, and so forth, to cultivate minors' awareness of network security, civility, behavioral habits, and defensive skills.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 14:
People's governments at the county level or above shall make rational plans and a reasonable setup to promote the balanced and coordinated development of non-profit internet service, and strengthen the establishment of public cultural facilities that provide non-profit internet service, improving the conditions for minors going online.
Local people's governments at the county level or above shall provide high-quality internet literacy classes to students through methods such as allocating guidance teachers who have corresponding professional aptitudes to primary and secondary schools and through government procurement of services or encouraging primary and secondary schools to procure relevant services themselves.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 15:
Schools, communities, libraries, cultural centers, youth activity centers, and other such venues providing minors with internet access facilities, shall provide guidance and a safe and healthy environment for minors going online through methods such as arranging professionals or recruiting volunteers, as well as installing software for the protection of minors online or employing other technological safety measures.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 16:
Schools shall include content such as increasing internet literacy in learning and teaching activities, and reasonably use the networks to carry out teaching activities, shall establish and complete management systems for students going online during school, regulate smart terminals brought to school by minor students in accordance with law, help students form positive habits in going online, cultivate student's awareness of online safety and law, and enhance students ability to obtain, analyze, and assess online information.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 17:
Minors' guardians shall strengthen family education and family environments, increase their internet literacy, regulate their own internet usage, and strengthen education, modeling, guidance, and oversight for minors' internet usage.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 18:
The state encourages and supports the research, development, production, and use of specialized online technologies, products, and services for minors, such as online protection software or smart terminal products and minors modes or dedicated areas for minors, that are suited to rules and characteristics of minors' healthy physical and psychological development; and encourages the establishment and building of a barrier-free accessible internet, to promote minors broadening their horizons, molding their integrity, and improving their character.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 19:
Software for the protection of minors online and smart terminal products that are especially for minors shall possess effective functions such as for identifying illegal information and information that might impact minors' physical and psychological health, protecting minor's rights and interests in personal information, preventing minors from becoming addicted to the internet, and making guardians perform their guardianship duties.
In conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, the State Internet Information Office is to clarify the relevant technical standards and requirements for software for the protection of minors online and smart terminal products that are especially for minors, as needed for efforts to protect minors online, and is to guide and oversee relevant online industry organizations in conducting assessments of these methods in accordance with the relevant technical standards and requirements.
Producers of smart terminal products shall install software for the protection of minors before the products leave the factory, or employ noticeable methods to inform users about the channels and methods for installing the software. Sellers of smart terminal products shall employ noticeable methods to inform users about the installation of software for the protection of minors online as well as channels and methods for installation.
The guardians of minors shall reasonably use and guide minors to use the online protection software, smart terminal products, and so forth, to create a positive family environment for internet use.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 21:
The state encourages and supports the creation, reproduction, publication, and dissemination of online information that carries forward the Core Socialist Values and advanced socialist culture, revolutionary culture, and the exceptional traditional Chinese culture; solidifies the sense of community among the Chinese people, cultivates minors feelings for their home country and their good moral character, and guides minors to cultivate positive habits in their lives and conduct; to create a clean cyberspace and online ecology that is conducive to minors' healthy development.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 22:
Online information with content that is harmful to the physical or psychological health of minors such as promoting obscenity, pornography, violence, cults, superstitions, gambling, inducements to self-harm and suicide, terrorism, separatism, or extremism, must not be produced, reproduced, published, or transmitted by any organization or individual.
Pornographic and obscene online information related to minors must not be produced, reproduced, published, transmitted, or possessed by any organization or individual.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 23:
Where online products or services contain information that might lead or entice minors to imitate unsafe conduct, carry out conduct that violates social mores, cause extreme feelings, form bad habits, or that might otherwise impact minors' physical or psychological health, the organizations or individuals producing, reproducing, publishing, or transmitting them shall give conspicuous warnings before displaying the content.
In conjunction with the State Administration for Press and Publication, Film Department, and the State Council departments for education, communications, public security, culture and tourism, radio and television, and so forth, the State Internet Information Office is to determine the specific types, scope, assessment standards and warning methods for information that might impact minors' physical or psychological health on the foundation of the preceding paragraph.

instrument: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council; Decree 766 per secondary sources)
text:
Article 24:
Information that might impact minors' physical or psychological health as provided for in the first paragraph of article 23 of these Regulations must not be produced, reproduced, published, or transmitted in online products or services aimed at minors by any organization or individual.
The providers of online products and services must not embed information that might impact minors' physical or psychological health as provided for in the first paragraph of article 23 of these regulations in eye-catching positions in products or services or in key areas that easily draw in users such as home pages, initial pop-up windows, hot searches, and so forth.
Online product and service providers must not conduct commercial marketing to minors through automated decision-making.
